title: Sleep and wake: do not kill a healthy role for time the machine slept, and show how long work has run
lead: When the machine sleeps, the hung-role watchdog must not count the sleep as silence, so a wake no longer kills every healthy running role. `ork status` also shows how long a role or the checks step has run, how long ago the role last sent output, and how long the machine slept during that work.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Wave 4 (S100 and S207 run by ork itself, 2026-11-02; log `.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F12, F15-F17, F21, F22) lost work to machine sleep. Clock jumps seen by the owner: 20:59 to 23:02, 23:02 to 01:21, 01:21 to 06:55 EST. The S207 implementer was killed as `hung: no output for 30m` three times, and the S100 fix round once. Each kill needed a hand `ork retry`. The owner got no hint that the machine had slept.

Verified against HEAD of main (9202ba8):

- The watchdog compares `w.now().Sub(w.last)` with the limit (`internal/engine/watchdog.go:91`). `w.now` is `Deps.now`, which returns `time.Now().UTC()` (`internal/engine/engine.go:64-69`). The `time` package documents that `UTC` strips the monotonic clock reading (`go doc -all time`, section "Monotonic Clocks"), so the subtraction is wall-clock time. A sleep of an hour is one hour of silence. The next tick after the wake (every `min(limit/4, 30s)`, `watchdog.go:73-74`) sees more than 30 minutes and calls `kill()` (`watchdog.go:95-97`). That matches the log: the kill came at wake time, 64 minutes after the role started, with no output in between.
- The 30-minute limit is fixed by the owner (2026-10-29, `docs/design.md:770-773`). This slice does not change the limit.
- The project check timeout is not shown to count sleep. `runChecks` passes `CheckMinutes` (default 10 minutes) to `clirun.Run`, which uses `context.WithTimeout` (`internal/engine/states.go:193-203`, `internal/clirun/clirun.go:129`). That is a Go timer, not a wall-clock comparison. The log shows no check killed by a sleep: the S100 check was still running 64 minutes after it started (F13), and `go test`'s own `-timeout` did not fire either (F17). The project's `check_minutes` for ork was not read, so whether that run was past its ork timeout is not known. So this slice leaves the check timeout alone and only reports how long a check has run. F12's claim about the check timeout is not supported by the code.
- The orphaned `go test` processes (F15, F16) are a separate problem with a separate fix; see the slice `reap-process-tree`.
- `ork status` prints no start time, elapsed time or last-output age for a running role or a checks step (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:79-96` prints id, item, state, wait, denials and error only). The role's `started_at` is in `--json` (`roles[]`, `internal/source/source.go:253`), but the checks step has no start time anywhere, and the last-output time lives only in `roleWatch.last` in memory (`watchdog.go:45`).
- `docs/guide.md:395` says "ork does not retry for you". The owner decided on 2026-11-02 that ork does not retry a hung kill by itself; this slice does not change it.

Design choices (owner, interactive question, 2026-11-02): sleep is found by a wall-clock gap between samples taken about every 5 seconds (no cgo); one shared detector lives in the daemon; slept time is kept in memory and status only, not in `run.json`; ork does not retry a hung kill by itself.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Engine, in `internal/engine/wake_test.go`:

- `TestWakeCountsAWallClockJumpAsSleep`: a `Wake` built on a fake clock that advances 5 seconds per step; one step of 2 hours. `Slept()` returns the jump minus one step. It fails first because `Wake` does not exist.
- `TestWakeIgnoresASmallStall`: a step of 10 seconds (under the 30-second threshold) adds nothing.
- `TestWakeSampleIsSynchronous`: `Slept()` called right after a jump, before the background tick runs, already includes the jump (so the watchdog cannot see the jump first and kill).
- `TestWakeNilCountsNothing`: a nil `*Wake` returns zero and does not panic (tests and tools that do not set `Deps.Wake`).
- `TestWakeStartSamplesInTheBackground`: after `Start`, the background sampler alone sees a jump.

Engine, in `internal/engine/watchdog_test.go`:

- `TestWakeJumpDoesNotKillASilentRole`: `Deps.Now` is `time.Now` plus an atomic offset; `Deps.Wake` shares that clock; `HungAfter` is 250 ms and the role is silent. After 100 ms the test adds 1 hour to the offset. The role ends 100 ms later (200 ms of real silence, under the limit). It must not be killed; the test requires state `awaiting-approval` and no `hung` role record. It fails first because the watchdog compares wall time and kills at the next tick.
- `TestSilenceAfterAWakeStillKills`: same setup; after the jump the role stays silent for the full limit; it must be killed, with reason text `hung: no output for` the limit. This proves the fix does not turn the watchdog off.
- `TestSilenceBeforeAWakeIsStillCounted`: the role is silent for 150 ms, then the jump, then silent: killed about 100 ms after the jump, because the earlier silence still counts.
- `TestEventAfterAWakeResetsTheSilence`: a jump, then an event, then silence for less than the limit: not killed.
- `TestSilenceAfterAnEventAfterAWakeStillKills`: a jump, then an event, then silence for the full limit: killed a full limit after the event.
- `TestSleepBeforeTheRoleStartedDoesNotHideAHang`: a jump before the round starts; the silent role is still killed.
- `TestWatchdogWithoutWakeKeepsTheOldBehaviour`: `Deps.Wake` nil: the existing tests in this file must still pass unchanged, and a jump kills a silent role (documents the nil case).

Working snapshot, in `internal/engine/wake_test.go` (`Engine.Working()` takes no argument):

- `TestWorkingNamesARunningRoleWithItsLastOutputAndSleep`: a blocked fake role; `Engine.Working()` returns one entry with `What` "implementer round 1", `Since` equal to the round start, `LastOutput` equal to the last `OnEvent`, and `Slept` equal to the jump seen since the start (a sleep before the start is not counted).
- `TestWorkingNamesTheChecksStep`: a blocked fake `Deps.Check`; `Working` returns "checks" with `Since` set and a zero `LastOutput`.
- `TestWorkingIsEmptyWhenNothingRuns`: after the round and after the checks end, `Working` is empty (the entry is removed even on error and cancel).
- `TestWorkingListsTheReviewerAndTheUIPassTogether`: the two review roles in one state give two entries in a fixed order (role name).

Daemon, in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`:

- `TestStatusCarriesWorkingForARunningRun`: the run row of a run whose role is blocked has `working[0].what`, `since` and `last_output`; a run at rest has no `working` key; every run shares one `Wake`.

CLI, in `internal/cli/run_test.go`:

- `TestStatusPrintsWorkingTimes`: with `App.Now` fixed, a run row with `working` prints `    working: implementer round 2, 14m (last output 2m ago, slept 1h03m)` under the run line and before the `error:` line. The duration helper prints seconds under a minute, `Nm` under an hour and `NhMMm` above, as step 7 says (the earlier example `slept 63m` disagreed with it).
- `TestStatusPrintsEachWorkingEntry`: two entries print two lines, seconds under a minute.
- `TestStatusPrintsChecksWorkingWithoutLastOutput`: `    working: checks, 12m` (no last-output clause when `last_output` is absent; no slept clause when zero).
- `TestStatusWorkingJSONKeepsTheTimes`: `--json` carries `since`, `last_output` and `slept_seconds`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
The steps follow the owner's answers of 2026-11-02 (see the design choices in the lead section).

1. Tests first from the failing list. Run `go -C WORKTREE test ./internal/engine -run 'Wake|Working|Hung|Silent'` and confirm each new test fails for the reason given.
2. `internal/engine/wake.go`: type `Wake` with a mutex, a `now func() time.Time`, the time of the last sample, and the total `slept`. `NewWake(now func() time.Time)` and `Start(ctx)` run a goroutine that samples every 5 seconds. `sample()` takes the lock, reads `now`, and if the wall gap since the last sample is over 30 seconds it adds `gap - 5s` to `slept`; it then stores `now`. `Slept()` calls `sample()` first and returns the total, so a caller never reads a total that lacks a jump it has already crossed. A nil `*Wake` returns zero from `Slept()` and does nothing in `Start`. The 5 s and 30 s values are named constants. (detect by a wall-clock gap between samples. It works whether or not the platform's monotonic clock counts sleep, and needs only the standard library on macOS and Linux.)
3. `internal/engine/engine.go`: add `Wake *Wake` to `Deps` with a one-line comment; nil means sleep is not detected. `internal/daemon/runs.go` `initRunManager`: when `deps.Wake` is nil build one with the daemon clock (`d.cfg.Clock.Now`) and start it with the run manager's context, so every run shares it (as `Vendors` is shared, `runs.go:162-168`). Stop it when the manager closes.
4. `internal/engine/watchdog.go`: give `roleWatch` the `*Wake` and the slept total at the last sign of life. `touch` stores both. The silence is `now.Sub(last) - (wake.Slept() - sleptAtLast)`; kill only when that is over the limit. Read `Slept()` under `w.mu` together with `now`; `Slept()` samples first, so the comparison never sees a jump the total lacks. `watchRole` records the total at start. Keep `hungReason` unchanged (it names the limit). Do not change `DefaultHungAfter`, the tick rate or the kill path.
5. `Engine` working registry: a small struct with its own mutex (as `vendorWait` has, `engine.go:129`, because `Run` holds `e.mu`). `runRound` adds an entry just before `Runner.Run` with `What` `"<role> round <n>"`, `Since` `e.d.now()`, the watch (for `LastOutput`) and the slept total at start; it removes the entry with `defer`. `runChecks` adds `"checks"` (or `"<prefix>"` if `prefix` is not `checks`; read the callers) and removes it with `defer`. `Engine.Working(now)` returns entries sorted by `What` as `[]Working{What, Since, LastOutput, Slept}`; `Slept` is `wake.Slept()` minus the total at start. `LastOutput` is read from the watch under its lock and is zero when the watchdog is off or for a check.
6. `internal/source/source.go`: `EngineWork{What string; Since time.Time; LastOutput time.Time (omitzero); SleptSeconds int}` and `EngineRun.Working []EngineWork` with `json:"working,omitempty"` and a comment "proposed: daemon memory only". `internal/daemon/runs.go:1312-1318`: fill it from `m.engine.Working` for a run whose engine is loaded and busy. Nothing is written to `run.json`. (Q3 a.)
7. `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go`: after the run line (and before the `error:` line), print `    working: WHAT, ELAPSED` and, when present, ` (last output AGE ago, slept SLEPT)` with the clauses that apply. Use a small local duration helper that prints seconds under a minute, `Nm` under an hour and `NhMMm` above; do not import `internal/tui`. `App.Now` supplies the clock; `Run` sets nothing when it is nil.
8. Docs: `docs/design.md` Hung role item gets two sentences (time the machine slept is not counted; a wake alone does not kill a role; the detector is a wall-clock gap between samples, *proposed*). Mirror in `docs/guide.md:395` and `docs/dashboard.md:543`; `docs/state.md` gets a sentence that nothing about sleep is stored. Add the `status` working line to the CLI section of `docs/design.md` if one lists the status output (check with `rg -n "needs you" docs/design.md docs/guide.md`).
9. Do not touch the 30-minute limit, the project check timeout, `clirun`, the vendor adapters, `internal/tui`, `internal/engine/recover.go`, or any retry behaviour.
10. Add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry last, under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*: "Do not count machine sleep as silence for the hung-role watchdog; show working time, last output and slept time in `ork status`."
11. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=3 ./internal/engine -run 'Wake|Working|Hung|Silent'` (the jump tests use real timers; three runs catch flakiness).
- `rg -n "Wake" internal/daemon/runs.go` shows one shared value built once in `initRunManager`.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] Start a real run, close the lid or run `pmset sleepnow` for longer than the hung limit (35 minutes is enough proof), wake the machine, and confirm that the role is still running, `ork status` shows `slept` for it, and no `hung` pause appears.
- [HUMAN CHECK] `ork status` on a live run at 100 columns: the working line wraps cleanly under the run row.
